definitions.explanation: A person who pulls a jinrikisha (人力車), a two-wheeled passenger cart. Historically a common occupation in the Meiji through early Shōwa periods. Today, rickshaw pullers can still be seen in tourist areas like Asakusa, Kyoto, and Kamakura.

examples.japanese: {車夫|しゃふ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{観光客|かんこうきゃく}→観光客：03022_kankoukyaku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{乗|の}せて→乗せる：01972_noseru⟧⟦{走|はし}る→走る：00519_hashiru⟧。
examples.english: The rickshaw puller runs carrying tourists.

examples.japanese: ⟦{浅草|あさくさ}→浅草：28393_asakusa⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{車夫|しゃふ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{案内|あんない}して→案内する：20203_annaisuru⟧⟦もらった→もらう：00520_morau⟧。
examples.english: I had a rickshaw puller show me around in Asakusa.

examples.japanese: ⟦{明治時代|めいじじだい}→明治時代：28080_meijijidai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{小説|しょうせつ}→小説：01434_shousetsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{車夫|しゃふ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦よく→よく：00601_yoku⟧⟦{登場|とうじょう}→登場：13625_toujou⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: Rickshaw pullers frequently appear in novels from the Meiji era.

notes:
{車夫|しゃふ} literally means "vehicle man" (⟦{車|しゃ}→車：09874_sha⟧ = vehicle, {夫|ふ} = man/laborer). The full term for the vehicle is ⟦{人力車|じんりきしゃ}→人力車：11472_jinrikisha⟧ (human-powered vehicle). Modern rickshaw pullers in tourist areas are often athletic young people who also serve as tour guides.
